blocks.content: Quiz: Why is the fetch() function used asynchronously in JavaScript?
Tap an option below to answer:
Because it sends a request and blocks the rest of your code until a response is received.
fetch() doesn't block the rest of your code.
fetch() doesn't block the rest of your code.
Because it sends a request and doesn't block the rest of your code from running while it waits for a response.
fetch() sends a request and runs the rest of the code asynchronously.
fetch() sends a request and runs the rest of the code asynchronously.
Because it always requires a callback function to handle the response.
fetch() doesn't always require callback. It sends the request and runs the rest of the code asynchronously.
fetch() doesn't always require callback. It sends the request and runs the rest of the code asynchronously.
Because it automatically retries the request if it fails.
fetch() doesn't automatically retry the request if it fails. It runs the rest of the code after sending a request.
fetch() doesn't automatically retry the request if it fails. It runs the rest of the code after sending a request.
